payload.goal: Make record-hygiene D1's self-recording exemption quote-aware: splitting on shell operators without honouring quotes means any commit whose message has a body (this repo's own convention) is logged as command_run, so the working tree is dirty the instant it is clean and every session opens with a false staleness warning. Restore the exemption's stated invariant — ambiguity resolves toward logging, never toward swallowing real work.

plan.goal: Make record-hygiene D1's self-recording exemption quote-aware, so committing the record with a multi-line message (this repo's own convention) appends no command_run and the tree can settle — without weakening the invariant that ambiguity resolves toward logging.

tasks.title: Quote-aware operator scan in isSelfRecordingCommand: split on &&, ||, ;, |, newline only outside single/double quotes, honouring backslash escapes; unbalanced quotes fall back to logging
Close the command-substitution hole in the same scan: $( or backtick in unquoted text makes the command non-exempt (today `git log $(rm -rf x)` is exempt)
Tests in hooks.test.ts: multi-line commit message exempt, quoted && exempt, unbalanced quotes logged, substitution logged, pipes/echo still logged
SPEC §PostToolUse (lines 772-781) reworded off 'quote-unaware', plus the Decision entry the deviation requires

payload.because: Quote-unawareness was never conservatism — a && or newline inside a quoted string is not a separator, so reading it as one is simply wrong, and it happened to fail toward logging by accident rather than design. The cost was concrete: this repo's own multi-line commit messages defeated the exemption, so the record could not settle and every session opened with a false staleness warning. The two extra holes are the same defect in the other direction — `git log $(rm -rf x)` rode the leading git to an exemption, swallowing real work — and closing them in the same scan is what makes "ambiguity resolves toward logging" true as stated instead of accidental.
payload.chose: A quote-aware character scan (shellSegments) that splits only on separators appearing outside quotes, and returns "cannot scan" — resolved toward logging — for unbalanced quotes and for command substitution ($( or backtick outside single quotes). It also treats a lone & as a separator unless it belongs to a >&/<& redirect.
payload.over: Keeping the quote-unaware regex split that SPEC lines 779-781 documented as deliberate conservatism; and, as a narrower option, honouring quotes only while leaving the substitution and background-& holes open.
